# #3906 — "Compiler infinite loop issue"

Filed 2021-08-13 by @hannes-vernooij. Labels `bug`, `crash`. One maintainer comment,
2024-04-18 by @damyanp: *"Setting to Dormant as there's a workaround for this."* Still open.

**Verdict: `repros`.** The shader in the issue body still fails to compile on every DXC that
was measured: all 20 catalogued stable releases from v1.4.1907 (2019) to v1.9.2607 (2026), and
the ground-truth build of `main`. Nothing about it has improved in the five years since it was
filed, and the defect it lands on is older than the oldest release in the catalogue.

## Ground truth

| | |
|---|---|
| compiler id | `main-debug` |
| build | clean Debug build of `main` |
| public commit | `13730886e` ("Improve Copilot release note review guidance (#8733)", 2026-08-06) |
| `dxc --version` | `dxcompiler.dll: 1.10(5433-ab540090)(1.9.0.5433) - 1.9.0.5433 (triage, ab5400907)` |

The version string self-reports `ab5400907`, which is a **fork-local** SHA with no public
existence; `13730886e` is the public commit the tree corresponds to. Captured output is left
exactly as the compiler produced it — it is evidence — so `ab5400907` appears verbatim in the
`out-*.txt` files and is *not* an inconsistency.

Tree equivalence was checked rather than assumed: `git diff --name-only 13730886e HEAD` lists
zero files outside the triage skill directory. As a control that the query can see differences
at all, `git diff --name-only 13730886e~50 13730886e` lists 140 files outside it.

## Repro

`repro.hlsl` is the shader from the issue body, verbatim. `cmd.txt` is `-T cs_6_0 -E main
repro.hlsl`.

**Repro quality: `complete`** — the full shader is inline in the issue.

**The command line is not.** The issue's only pointer to it was a `shader-playground.timjones.io`
permalink, and that host no longer resolves (DNS failure, checked 2026-08-10), so the reporter's
exact arguments are unrecoverable. The profile and entry point are derived from the source, not
guessed: the shader declares `[numthreads(8, 8, 1)] void main(...)` taking `SV_DispatchThreadID`,
so the stage is compute and the entry is `main`. `cs_6_0` is the oldest compute profile DXC has,
per the skill's "target the oldest profile that still shows the symptom".

The language-version question raised in `expected.md` turned out to be moot: no compiler in the
scan rejected the source, so `-HV 2018` was never needed and there are no `invalid-probe`s in
the history. The dead permalink is precisely why the Compiler Explorer link below has value — it
restores a runnable, third-party-hosted reproduction to an issue that had lost one.

## Predicate

`match.json` is `any_of[timeout, internal_failure]`, **pre-registered in `expected.md` before
any compiler was run.**

This was insurance against a hazard, not a prediction, and the hazard fired. Ground truth does
**not** time out — it exits `3758096385` (`0xE0000001`) in about a second with `Internal
compiler error: LLVM Assert`. Scored with a bare `timeout` predicate, `main-debug` would have
read `no-repro` against 20 timing-out releases, and this open, always-reproducing bug would have
been written up as **fixed**. The disjunction is the only reason the correct answer came out.

Both arms fired, on disjoint sets of compilers, and they are the same defect (proved below):

| arm | fires on | signature |
|---|---|---|
| `timeout` | all 20 stable releases | never terminates |
| `internal_failure` | `main-debug` | `0xE0000001`, `Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert` |

## What was run

**21 scored probes** (`out-main-debug.txt`, `out-v1.4.1907.txt` … `out-v1.9.2607.txt`) — every
one `repro`, no `invalid-probe`s. Produced by `triage.py bisect --issue 3906 --linear`; linear
rather than binary because every hanging probe costs the full 60 s bound and the first and last
releases both reproduced, so there was no window to bisect. Five probeable prereleases were
excluded by policy; `v1.2.0-alpha` was skipped for lack of a usable `dxc` asset.

History: **always repro'd across v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607.**

**8 variant probes** (`variant-*-main-debug.txt`) — three controls, four reduction steps and the
reporter's workaround, below.

**5 manual cases**, all generated by `make-manual-cases.py`, which is committed next to its
output and echoes every command through `subprocess.list2cmdline` so a reader can re-derive the
files instead of trusting a transcription:

- `manual-case-assert-stack.txt` — the full Debug assert stack under `cdb`.
- `manual-case-assert-identity.txt` — which assert each of the 9 shaders trips.
- `manual-case-condition-matrix.txt` — all 9 shaders × {v1.6.2106, v1.9.2607}, Release builds.
- `manual-case-long-timeout.txt` — the same command with a 600 s bound instead of 60 s.
- `manual-case-cpu-sample.txt` — CPU-time sampling of the hanging child process.

## The two signatures are one defect

This is the part that is *proved* rather than inferred, and it is what licenses reporting a
Debug assert as a reproduction of a reported hang.

`dxc` prints only `Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert` to stderr, so the scored captures
cannot tell two different asserts apart. Running under `cdb` gives the identity
(`manual-case-assert-identity.txt`, `manual-case-assert-stack.txt`). On `repro.hlsl`, two
asserts fire in a chain — the first stopping the process, and the second reached by continuing
past it (`gh`, "go handled", which emulates what a Release build does when the assert is not
compiled in):

```
Error: assert(0 && "Type mismatch.")
File: <repo>\lib\Transforms\Scalar\ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp(2662)
Func: `anonymous-namespace'::SROA_Helper::RewriteBitCast
(68e8.7c5c): Unknown exception - code e0000001 (first chance)

Error:  !(&TheUse != PrevUse)
File: <repo>\lib\Transforms\Scalar\ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp(2996)
Func: `anonymous-namespace'::SROA_Helper::RewriteForScalarRepl.
        Infinite loop while SROA'ing value, use isn't getting eliminated.
(68e8.7c5c): Break instruction exception - code 80000003 (first chance)
```

The second assert's message is the reported symptom, named by DXC's own diagnostic. Frames, in
order: `SROA_Parameter_HLSL::runOnModule` → `SROAGlobalAndAllocas` → `DoScalarReplacement` →
`RewriteForScalarRepl` → `RewriteForGEP` → `RewriteForScalarRepl` → `RewriteBitCast`.

The source says why the Release build spins where the Debug build stops
(`lib/Transforms/Scalar/ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp`):

```cpp
2661:   if (!SrcTy->isStructTy()) {
2662:     assert(0 && "Type mismatch.");
2663:     return;
2664:   }
```

```cpp
2991:   while (!V->use_empty()) {
2992:     Use &TheUse = *V->use_begin();
2993:
2994:     DXASSERT_LOCALVAR(
2995:         PrevUse, &TheUse != PrevUse,
2996:         "Infinite loop while SROA'ing value, use isn't getting eliminated.");
2997:     PrevUse = &TheUse;
2998:
2999:     // Each of these must either call ->eraseFromParent()
3000:     // or null out the use of V so that we make progress.
```

Under `NDEBUG`, `assert` expands to nothing and **the bare `return;` at 2663 stays**. The
comment at 2999-3000 states the contract the bail-out breaks: it neither erases the bitcast nor
nulls the use, so `V->use_empty()` is never satisfied and `*V->use_begin()` hands back the same
use forever. The guard that would catch that is `DXASSERT_LOCALVAR`, which
`include/dxc/Support/Global.h` (~line 362) expands under `NDEBUG` to `do { (void)(local); }
while (0)`. Both guards vanish in a Release build; the loop remains. That is the infinite loop.

This is not a "silent only because it is a Debug assert" artefact — the Release builds really do
hang, which the 20-release scan and the 600 s manual case measure directly.

**Provenance of the code.** `git log --all -S` (repository-wide, not scoped to the current path,
which would only see the 2023 clang-format move `37ed61386`):

| element | commit | date | in v1.4.1907? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `assert(0 && "Type mismatch.")` bail-out | `6ee4074a4` "first commit" | 2016-12-28 | yes |
| `"Infinite loop while SROA'ing value…"` guard | `69c685f3e` | 2019-02-24 | yes |
| `onlyUsedByLifetimeMarkers` DXASSERT (2629) | `eaa7f95d0` (#3034, lifetime intrinsics) | 2020-11-17 | no (first in v1.6.2104) |

The bail-out that causes the hang predates every probeable release by two and a half years,
which is consistent with "always repro'd" rather than merely compatible with it.

## Controls: two of three predictions were wrong

The report states three conditions and says *"when any of these steps are missing it will not
result in an infinite loop"*. That is a ready-made control suite — far stronger than a generic
hello-world control, because it claims the predicate should flip on a named axis. Three
controls were built, one per condition, each declared `--expect no-match` **before** running:

| control | condition removed | main-debug | v1.6.2106 | v1.9.2607 | predicted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `control-no-member-fn.hlsl` | index no longer from a member fn (`this.h.handle`) | assert | HANG | HANG | ✗ wrong |
| `control-no-buffer-access.hlsl` | no `ByteAddressBuffer` subscript | assert | HANG | HANG | ✗ wrong |
| `control-scalar-return.hlsl` | returns `float3`, not `float3[2]` | exit 0 | exit 0 | exit 0 | ✓ |

Two of three predictions were falsified. The declarations were corrected with
`triage.py expect --issue 3906 --capture … --expect match`, which rewrites the declaration and
leaves the measurement untouched; the reasons are recorded in the capture headers.

The suite still does its job: `control-scalar-return.hlsl` is a near neighbour of the repro —
same struct, same member function, same buffer access, one return type changed — and it scores
`no-match`. The predicate discriminates. It just discriminates on a narrower axis than the
report describes.

**Note the dates and be careful about what this means.** v1.6.2106 shipped 2021-07-01, six weeks
*before* the 2021-08-13 report, and the reporter says they used "latest from master", i.e.
somewhere between v1.6.2106 and v1.6.2112 — both of which hang on all three of my variants. But
these are *my* reconstructions of "condition removed", not the reporter's shaders, and their
versions are not recoverable. The honest statement is about the two configurations that were
measured, and no more: **the shader as filed reproduces, and so do variants with conditions 1
and 2 removed.** Nothing here needs the reporter to have been wrong, and the write-up does not
say they were.

## Reduction

Continuing to cut (`reduce-*.hlsl`, all four also run against both Release builds in
`manual-case-condition-matrix.txt`):

| shader | shape | main-debug | v1.6.2106 / v1.9.2607 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reduce-nested-struct-member.hlsl` | struct with a **struct-typed** member; array-returning member fn; no buffer, no `readIndex()` | `0xE0000001` | HANG / HANG |
| `reduce-scalar-member.hlsl` | same, member flattened to a bare `uint` | `0x80000003` | *different signature*, see below |
| `reduce-member-array-return.hlsl` | struct with **no** data member; array-returning member fn | exit 0 | exit 0 / exit 0 |
| `reduce-free-array-return.hlsl` | **free** function returning an array | exit 0 | exit 0 / exit 0 |

`reduce-member-array-return.hlsl` was declared `--expect match` and scored `no-repro`; that
declaration was corrected too. It is the useful negative: an array-returning member function is
*not* sufficient on its own — the struct must also have a data member.

**Smallest measured shape that reproduces the hang** (`reduce-nested-struct-member.hlsl`) — no
`ByteAddressBuffer`, no `register`, no `readIndex()`, no shader-model-specific feature:

```hlsl
struct RenderResourceHandle { uint handle; };

struct Test {
    RenderResourceHandle h;
    float3 infLoop()[2] {
        uint i = this.h.handle;
        float3 v[2] = { 0.xxx, 0.xxx };
        return v;
    }
};

[numthreads(8, 8, 1)] void main() {
    Test t;
    t.h.handle = 0;
    float3 w[2] = t.infLoop();
}
```

## A neighbouring, distinct signature — do not fold it in

`reduce-scalar-member.hlsl` (the same shader with `RenderResourceHandle h;` flattened to
`uint h;`) does **not** hang. It trips a different assert — `!(onlyUsedByLifetimeMarkers(BCI))`
at `ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp(2630)`, *"expected struct bitcast to only be used by lifetime
intrinsics"* — and on Release builds it fails fast rather than looping:

| compiler | exit | text |
|---|---|---|
| main-debug | `0x80000003` (`__debugbreak`) | `Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert` |
| v1.6.2106 | `0x80AA001D` (`DXC_E_LLVM_CAST_ERROR`) | `Internal Compiler error: llvm::cast<X>() argument of incompatible type!` |
| v1.9.2607 | `0x80004005` (`E_FAIL`) | `error: llvm::cast<X>() argument of incompatible type!` |

Both are `internal_failure` under the predicate, so `--expect match` on that variant is correct,
but the *mechanism* differs and it is a different bug shape. It is the other early exit from the
same function: `RewriteBitCast` bails at `!DstTy->isStructTy()` (2624) into the
lifetime-intrinsic path and hits a hard `cast<>` failure, instead of bailing at
`!SrcTy->isStructTy()` (2661) and returning without progress. That difference is exactly why one
terminates and the other does not. It is recorded here so that a fix is validated against both
shapes, and deliberately **not** merged into the headline finding.

## Compiler Explorer

**https://godbolt.org/z/M7Ex1s9b3** — verified by reading the shortlink back
(`GET /api/shortlinkinfo/M7Ex1s9b3`). Full pane output in
`manual-case-godbolt-verify.txt`.

| pane | args | result |
|---|---|---|
| `dxc_1_6_2112` | `-T cs_6_0 -E main` | exit 143, `Killed - processing time exceeded`, `SIGKILL` |
| `dxc_trunk` | `-T cs_6_0 -E main` | exit 143, `Killed - processing time exceeded`, `SIGKILL` |
| `hlsl_clang_trunk` | `-T cs_6_0 -E main` | exit 0, compiles cleanly |

Limitation, stated on the page in `godbolt-note.txt`: CE ships **Release builds only**, so it
shows the hang and can never show the assert. It corroborates the local Debug build; it does not
overrule it. The shader stores nothing, so a compiler that gets through it is expected to emit
an empty entry point — the empty body is not the bug, not terminating is.

`hlsl_clang_trunk` — the new Clang-based HLSL front end — compiles the same source without
incident. That is a genuine data point about where the defect lives (the DXC-specific
`SROA_Parameter_HLSL` pass, which has no counterpart there), and it means the `check-in-clang`
label would be asking for work that has already been done.

## Is the hang unbounded, or merely slow?

`triage.py` bounds every probe at a hard-coded 60 s (`TIMEOUT`, line 64; no CLI override), and a
60 s timeout alone cannot distinguish an infinite loop from a slow compile. Three independent
checks say unbounded, and say more than that:

- `manual-case-long-timeout.txt` — v1.9.2607 on `repro.hlsl` with a 600 s bound: `STILL RUNNING
  AFTER 600s -- killed by the harness`. Ten minutes on a 30-line shader with no loops in it.
- `manual-case-cpu-sample.txt` — the same run, sampling the child's kernel+user CPU through
  `GetProcessTimes`. `cpu/elapsed` reads **1.00 at every sample across 90 s**. This is a *spin*,
  not a deadlock and not an I/O wait — a distinction a timeout cannot make, and it rules out the
  "waiting on something" family of explanations entirely.
- The mechanism is a `while` loop whose exit condition provably cannot change, and DXC's own
  guard for that loop names it. This is not a slow algorithm; there is no progress to make.

## Assessment

Open, valid, reproducing on everything measured, with a mechanism identified in source and a
minimal repro attached. `still-valid-keep-open`, confidence **high**.

The 2024-04-18 comment setting the issue Dormant is about priority (a workaround exists), not
about validity, and nothing here contradicts it. The workaround the reporter gives — wrap the
values in a struct and return the struct — was **measured, not assumed**:
`workaround-struct-return.hlsl` is `repro.hlsl` with exactly that change and nothing else, and
it compiles to DXIL on `main-debug`, v1.6.2106 and v1.9.2607 (exit 0 in each case). It works
because it removes the array return, which the one correct control shows is the load-bearing
condition.

**Labels: no change proposed.** `bug` and `crash` are already on it. The taxonomy has no `hang`
label (58 labels, refreshed 2026-08-10), and `crash` is defined as "DXC crashing or hitting an
assert" — which is literally accurate for the Debug behaviour and the closest available fit for
the Release behaviour. `check-in-clang` would be a to-do label for work already done and
reported above.

**`text_stale`: not set,** deliberately, and this was a close call. The title, the reported
symptom, the repro and the workaround are all still exactly accurate — the issue reproduces as
filed. What does not hold is the reporter's *three-condition* characterisation, and that is a
reduction hypothesis rather than a description of compiler behaviour. Setting `text_stale` would
also require asserting that the reporter's own variants behaved as mine do, on a version I
cannot recover, which the evidence does not support. The condition matrix is reported in the
draft comment as a measurement, which is where it is useful, without a staleness claim on top.
